ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

domain_restrictions: A,B,d are integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0
Empty product convention: if d=0 then ∏_{i=1}^0 (...) = 1 so Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1
Assumption: the rational expression Q_{A,B,d}(q) is actually a polynomial, i.e., Q_{A,B,d}(q) ∈ Q[q] (not just a rational function)
Graded ring S is Q[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_i)=B+i for i=1..d
If d=0, interpret S as Q (no variables, hence no f_i witnesses needed)
Each f_i is homogeneous in S with weighted degree deg(f_i)=A+i
Regularity condition: in the successive quotient S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}), the class of f_i is not a zero-divisor (equivalently: (f_1,...,f_d) is a homogeneous regular sequence in S)
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Let A,B,d ∈ Z with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, and define Q_{A,B,d}(q)=∏_{i=1}^d (1-q^{A+i})/(1-q^{B+i}) with Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1. If Q_{A,B,d}(q) ∈ Q[q], then in the weighted graded polynomial ring S=Q[x_1,...,x_d] (or S=Q if d=0) with deg(x_i)=B+i, there exist homogeneous elements f_1,...,f_d ∈ S such that deg(f_i)=A+i for each i=1..d and for each i the class of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor (so f_1,...,f_d form a homogeneous regular sequence). Consequently, the graded data of S modulo this regular sequence yields the given expression Q_{A,B,d}(q) (as stated in the equivalence).

Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) := ∏_{i=1}^d (1-q^{A+i})/(1-q^{B+i}) belongs to Q[q] (q formal indeterminate)
There exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that for each i=1..d: deg(f_i)=A+i, and the image of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl:
We prove the statement directly.

If d = 0, there are no variables and no polynomials to choose. Affine 0-space consists of a single point, the origin, so the empty family already has common zero locus exactly the origin. Thus assume d >= 1.

Let kbar be an algebraic closure of k, and write [d] = {1,...,d}. For each i, let V_i be the k-vector space of weighted-homogeneous polynomials in S = k[x_1,...,x_d] of weighted degree e_i. Because all w_j are positive and e_i is fixed, there are only finitely many monomials of weighted degree e_i, so V_i is finite-dimensional. Also, taking J = [d] in the hypothesis, at least d of the d integers e_1,...,e_d lie in Sigma([d]); hence every e_i lies in Sigma([d]), so each V_i is nonzero. Set Vbar_i = V_i tensor_k kbar, set Vbar = Vbar_1 x ... x Vbar_d, and let N = dim(Vbar) = sum_i dim(V_i).

For a nonempty subset J of [d], define
A_J = { i in [d] : e_i belongs to Sigma(J) }
and r_J = |A_J|.
By hypothesis, r_J >= |J| for every nonempty J.

Now fix a nonempty J subset of [d] and an element a in J. Consider
U_{J,a} = { x in kbar^d : x_j = 0 for j not in J, x_a = 1, and x_j != 0 for j in J minus {a} }.
This is isomorphic to (kbar^*)^{|J|-1}, so dim(U_{J,a}) = |J|-1.

For each i in A_J, choose one monomial M_{i,J} involving only variables x_j with j in J and having weighted degree e_i; such a monomial exists by definition of Sigma(J). Since every coordinate indexed by J is nonzero on U_{J,a}, we have M_{i,J}(x) != 0 for all x in U_{J,a}. Choose a kbar-vector-space decomposition
Vbar_i = kbar M_{i,J} direct sum W_{i,J}.

Define the incidence set
I_{J,a} = { ((g_1,...,g_d), x) in Vbar x U_{J,a} : g_1(x)=...=g_d(x)=0 }.
We compute its dimension.

First, if i is not in A_J, then every weighted-homogeneous polynomial of degree e_i vanishes on U_{J,a}. Indeed, if some monomial of degree e_i used only variables from J, then e_i would lie in Sigma(J), contrary to i not in A_J. So every degree-e_i monomial uses some variable outside J, and hence vanishes on U_{J,a} because all such outside coordinates are 0.

Next, if i is in A_J, write uniquely
g_i = c_i M_{i,J} + h_i
with h_i in W_{i,J}. For fixed x in U_{J,a}, the equation g_i(x)=0 is equivalent to
c_i = - h_i(x) / M_{i,J}(x),
because M_{i,J}(x) is nonzero. Thus, once x and h_i are chosen, the coefficient c_i is uniquely determined.

Therefore I_{J,a} is isomorphic to
U_{J,a} x (product over i in A_J of W_{i,J}) x (product over i not in A_J of Vbar_i).
Hence
(dim I_{J,a})
= (|J|-1) + sum over i in A_J of (dim V_i - 1) + sum over i not in A_J of dim V_i
= N + |J| - 1 - r_J
<= N - 1,
because r_J >= |J|.

Let pi_{J,a} be the projection from Vbar x U_{J,a} to Vbar, and let B_{J,a} be the Zariski closure of pi_{J,a}(I_{J,a}). Since the dimension of an image is at most the dimension of the source, dim(B_{J,a}) <= N-1. So each B_{J,a} is a proper closed subset of the N-dimensional affine space Vbar.

There are only finitely many pairs (J,a), so
B = union of all B_{J,a}
is again a proper closed subset of Vbar.

Because k is infinite, V(k) is Zariski dense in Vbar; equivalently, no nonzero polynomial on affine N-space over kbar vanishes on all k-rational points. Therefore the nonempty open set Vbar minus B contains some k-rational point G = (g_1,...,g_d) with g_i in V_i. These g_i are weighted-homogeneous of degree e_i by construction.

We claim that over kbar their common zero locus is exactly the origin.

First, 0 is a common zero, because each e_i is positive, so each g_i has no constant term.

Now suppose x = (x_1,...,x_d) in kbar^d is a common zero with x != 0. Let
J = { j in [d] : x_j != 0 }.
Then J is nonempty. Choose a in J. Since kbar is algebraically closed and x_a != 0, there exists lambda in kbar with lambda^(w_a) = x_a^(-1). Set
y_j = lambda^(w_j) x_j  for 1 <= j <= d.
Because each g_i is weighted-homogeneous of degree e_i, we have
g_i(y_1,...,y_d) = lambda^(e_i) g_i(x_1,...,x_d) = 0.
Also y_a = 1, and y_j = 0 exactly when x_j = 0, so y belongs to U_{J,a}. Thus (G,y) lies in I_{J,a}, which means G belongs to pi_{J,a}(I_{J,a}), hence to B_{J,a}, hence to B. But G was chosen outside B, a contradiction.

So no nonzero common zero exists. Therefore the common zero locus of g_1,...,g_d in affine d-space over kbar is exactly the origin, as required.

payload.statement_nl: Let k be an infinite field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_j)=w_j. Let e_1,...,e_d be positive integers. For each subset J of {1,...,d}, define Sigma(J) := { sum_{j in J} m_j w_j : each m_j is a nonnegative integer }. Assume that for every nonempty subset J of {1,...,d}, at least |J| of the integers e_1,...,e_d belong to Sigma(J). Then there exist homogeneous polynomials g_1,...,g_d in S with deg(g_i)=e_i for each i such that, over an algebraic closure of k, the common zero locus of g_1,...,g_d in affine d-space is exactly the origin.

dependency_assessment.notes: Proof is self-contained modulo standard algebraic-geometry facts about dimensions of images and Zariski density over infinite fields.

detailed_findings.finding: The core incidence-variety dimension count is correct: for each nonempty J and a in J, the bad parameter set has dimension at most N-1 because r_J >= |J|.
detailed_findings.location: middle of proof, computation of dim(I_{J,a})

detailed_findings.finding: The passage from a nonzero common zero x to a point y in U_{J,a} via weighted scaling is valid and uses algebraic closure correctly.
The proof relies on the standard fact that k-rational points are Zariski dense in affine space over kbar when k is infinite; this is acceptable but left implicit.

result_payload.reason: The proof matches the lemma's Hall-type semigroup condition and gives a standard dimension-count construction of degree-prescribed weighted-homogeneous polynomials whose common zero locus over an algebraic closure is exactly the origin. The incidence varieties I_{J,a} are correctly analyzed, the dimension bound dim I_{J,a} <= N-1 follows from r_J >= |J|, and the union of bad loci is therefore a proper closed subset of the parameter space. Choosing a k-rational point outside this bad locus is justified by Zariski density of k-rational points in affine space over an algebraic closure when k is infinite. The final scaling argument using weighted homogeneity correctly shows any nonzero common zero would place the chosen tuple in one of the bad loci, contradiction. No forbidden or undeclared dependency usage was identified.
